# Bākula Sutta (MN 124 (PTS MN iii 124))

**ID:** MN 124 (PTS MN iii 124)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Bākula Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** With Bakkula
**PTS:** MN iii 124
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Because Bakkula's confession spans eighty years of monastic life, the sutta's internal chronology implies that it was delivered at least thirty-five years after the Buddha's Parinibbāna [Anālayo 2011]. In accord with this, the commentary *Papañcasūdanī* explicitly records that MN 124 was incorporated into the canon only during the second communal recitation (*saṅgīti*) [Anālayo 2011]. Structurally, MN 124 shares with the preceding *Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta* (MN 123) a repetitive refrain formula that records each marvellous quality (*acchariya-abbhuta*) as something kept in mind by reciters, a mnemonic technique suggested to have facilitated the admission and preservation of later additions within the oral transmission [Anālayo 2011].

**Sources**

- [Anālayo 2011] Anālayo, The Genesis of the Bodhisattva Ideal (2011) — Discussed Bakkula's eighty-year declaration, post-demise dating, second council inclusion in the commentary, and structural refrain parallels with MN 123.
- [Bodhi 2012] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Numerical Discourses of the Buddha (2012) — Identified the interlocutor as Acelakassapa and summarized his conversation with Bakkula in MN 124.
- [Ñāṇamoli 2010] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli, The Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga) (2010) — Noted the citation of MN 124 regarding Bakkula's complete freedom from sickness.
